summary: Verified backend security hardening (S3 brute-force lockout, S4 track throttle, S5 HTML injection safety) plus regression on login, contact messages, member signup, and protected routes. 10/10 pytest tests passed against public REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1041 lines — consider splitting into routers (auth, pages, members, messages, analytics) for maintainability.

Brute-force lockout keys on IP:email; behind a load balancer, x-forwarded-for is honored (good) but there is no cap on total unique-email lockouts per IP — could be abused as a DoS enumerator (low risk).
GeoIP call to ip-api.com is synchronous `requests.get` inside an async endpoint — blocks the event loop up to 3s. Move to httpx.AsyncClient or run_in_executor.
Track throttle uses a Mongo `find_one` per hit; consider a small in-process TTL cache for higher-traffic paths.
seed_data_creation: Tests created a few TEST_-prefixed contact messages and one pending member for verification (not cleaned up; low volume).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Security hardening (S3/S4/S5) fully verified via /app/backend/tests/test_security_hardening.py. Brute-force test uses random throwaway emails so the real admin is never locked. The success-clears-counter test performs 2 failed + 1 success + 4 more failed against admin@4a4dixhuit.org; if re-run rapidly, ensure a final successful login clears attempts (already done in the test). Public URL used: REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL from /app/frontend/.env.
